task:
You are working in a dedicated git worktree on your own branch, not in the user's checkout. Commit your work as you go, with clear messages; anything left uncommitted will not be visible to the user.

You will get a task given from another source, or appended here. If thats not the case report DONE every cycle

## This run specifically

Repository: /workspace/UsageFoundry (Xapicc/UsageFoundry) — Next.js 15 + TypeScript. Read CLAUDE.md first: it states the rule this issue is about, that every decision of this kind is a pure exported function with unit tests because its failure modes are silent and expensive.

Issue: #109 — "sweepPaused decides a parked fleet's fate and has no test at all"
URL: https://github.com/Xapicc/UsageFoundry/issues/109
Start with `gh issue view 109` and read it in full.

The defect: `sweepPaused` (src/lib/orchestrator.ts, around line 4840) is not exported, has no pure core, and has no test — while `selectPromotable`, `releasableRuns`, `haltPlan`, `planItem`, `landRefusal`, `planInstanceStep`, `blockSettlement` and `decideSchedule` are all pure exported functions with tests, on the rule CLAUDE.md states.

What to do: extract the decision out of `sweepPaused` into a pure, exported function named in the house style, and unit test it in src/lib/orchestrator.test.ts. It must cover all four branches the issue enumerates:
1. which parked runs are due (a null `resume_at` is due immediately);
2. cleared but the folder is taken → stay parked with the corrected reason, and **idempotently** — the guarded UPDATE is the whole reason this does not write a row and a log line every 60 seconds per parked run, and at 25 parked runs a regression is 25 rows a minute into `run_events`;
3. cleared and free → re-queue (through `promoteQueued`, not `startRun` — that is what keeps FIFO order, folder reservation and the concurrency cap in one place);
4. a verdict that can never clear → end the run rather than leave it holding a folder.

This is an extraction plus tests, not a behaviour change: the sweeper must do exactly what it does today. If you find a genuine bug while extracting, fix it only if it is unambiguous, and say so explicitly in the close comment.

Done looks like: the pure function is exported and covered, `npm run typecheck` passes, `npm test` passes, and the new tests fail against the old behaviour where they are meant to. Commit on your own branch as you go. Do not push, do not open a pull request, do not merge into main.

Then close the issue yourself: `gh issue close 109 --comment "..."` with what you changed, which files, what each new test pins, and how you verified it — name the commands you ran and their real result.

Last resort only: if the fix genuinely needs a decision you cannot make, stop at once — make no commits, restore the checkout with `git checkout -- . && git clean -fd`, post `gh issue comment 109 --body "..."` explaining what is blocked and what decision is needed, leave the issue open, and say in your final report that your branch is empty and should be purged.
